changes.current_line: Every payout reconciles automatically to its transactions and your ERP.
changes.change: For finance-led buyers (CFO, controller), lead with this line and say it their way: 'Know where your money is: every deposit matched to its transactions, invoices and your ERP, without a week of archaeology.' Say 'deposits' instead of 'payouts' with this buyer.
changes.why: Payout reconciliation was the only part of the pitch that got a reaction, and the decider talked about 'the deposits' and wanting to 'know where my money is', never 'payments' or 'payouts'.

changes.current_line: Proven ROI, backed by an independent economic impact study.
changes.change: For finance buyers, replace the study claim with an offer: 'Send us one month of your statements and we'll show what manual deposit matching costs you, in your numbers.'
changes.why: The deal went from 20 percent to won after the cost was rebuilt from the controller's own statements, and the CFO valued it because it was 'my number, not yours.'

changes.current_line: Financial infrastructure to grow globally, in every currency.
changes.change: Don't open first calls with this line for finance-led buyers whose business isn't global. Open with the deposit-matching line (M9) instead.
changes.why: The standard opener about 'global growth, all the currencies' got silence from a company that sells to restaurants in three states, and 'nobody said infrastructure.'

changes.current_line: Built for developers: launch payments fast with our APIs, docs and sandbox.
changes.change: When the signer is in finance, keep the developer and API message off the first call and off page one of the proposal. Move it to an appendix for IT.
changes.why: The portal-led proposal sent to IT was dismissed by the decider after one page as 'not her problem', and the IT team was not building anything for an API pitch to serve.
